messages:
mike: FYI saw a big perf delta on canary after yesterday's release. latency p95 up ~2x and compile churn spiked. looks like kernel-choice oscillation + kvcache evictions.
laura: ugh. do we have flamegraphs or profiler dumps? any obvious PRs to blame? :thinking_face: 
perf-ci-bot: [ALERT] canary-perf-check failed: p95_latency 210ms -> 420ms, compile-rate +350% (link: https://ci.redwood/mitigations/1781)
chris: starting a quick bisect across merges from last 24h. will post commit ranges.
mike: thanks. suspect heuristics change in the new selector rewrite (PR #3456) — it changed the score weighting for short vs long seqs. might have caused more kernel switches at runtime.
sara: PR #3456 also flipped the compile fallback to prefer newer kernels which might not be cached on nodes. that + smaller batch heuristics could explain evictions.
chris: bisect progress: tested commits a1f3..b5c2..d9e0 — perf stable until commit b5c2 (author: sara). repeating to confirm.
laura: can you paste the selector config from b5c2 and current? I want to diff.
chris: here are the relevant bits: ```
# b5c2 selector.conf
weights:
  short_seq: 0.6
  long_seq: 0.4
cache_policy: LRU
fallback: prefer_newer

# HEAD (post-merge)
weights:
  short_seq: 0.8
  long_seq: 0.2
cache_policy: LRU
fallback: prefer_newer
```
mike: note the short_seq increase — that will push more tiny requests to the smaller-kernel path, causing more kernel compiles when that kernel isn't resident. cumulative effect on shared nodes triggers cache thrash.
sara: confirmed locally: small synthetic workload shows compile-rate spike when short_seq weight >= 0.75. also saw kvcache miss-rate jump ~5x.
chris: holding canary rollback candidate. option A: revert the weight change. option B: change fallback to prefer_cached then prefer_newer.
laura: what's the rollout impact? Revert is fast but hides the selector improvements. prefer_cached seems safer, need tests.
mike: agree prefer_cached is less disruptive. patch suggestion posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3488 with tests and perf job.
perf-ci-bot: perf job queued (job id 1781-rc). expected runtime ~45m.
sara: if perf job passes, we can patch canary and monitor for one hour before wider rollout.
chris: also adding a short telemetry flag to record kernel-switch count per request (sampling 1%). will help quantify impact in prod.
mike: excellent. next steps: merge prefer_cached patch if CI green, enable telemetry, hold off on reverting until we see numbers. :thumbsup:
laura: adding this thread to the postmortem draft. thanks team.
perf-ci-bot: [UPDATE] perf job 1781-rc finished: p95_latency back to 205ms, compile-rate normalized.
mike: closing loop — canary patched, telemetry flagged, follow-up: revisit selector weights with more representative short/long seq distribution in benchmarks.
_meta: Generated Slack thread about kernel selection heuristic regression, compile churn, and KV cache eviction. Contains bisect notes, config diff, perf CI bot messages, and patch plan.
